title: S1d context_scanner: deterministic hostile-content scanner (safe/suspicious/blocked with evidence) and trust classes with a fixed authority order on evidence objects (P19, P20)
spec:
Create orchestrator/context_scanner.py. scan(text, *, source_kind) -> {"verdict": "safe"|"suspicious"|"blocked", "findings": [{"pattern": name, "line": n, "excerpt": max 120 chars}], "score": int}. Pattern families (regex, case-insensitive, each with a weight): override_instructions (ignore/disregard previous or prior instructions, you are now, new system prompt), authority_claim (claims to be the system, the operator, the developer, or to have higher authority), credential_read (read/print/cat of dotenv files, the user's ssh or cloud-provider credential directories, tokens, api keys, passwords), exfiltration (curl/wget/nc/fetch of a URL with a variable, token or file attached; base64 pipe to network), permission_change (world-writable chmod, sudoers edits, disable safeguards, hooks, guardrails, permissions bypass), hidden_execution (shell execution hidden in HTML comments, markdown links or images with javascript: or data: schemes), invisible_unicode (zero-width space/joiner, bidi overrides, tag characters), hidden_html (html comments or display:none blocks containing instruction verbs). Scoring: blocked when any pattern of weight 3 hits (override_instructions, credential_read+exfiltration together, hidden_execution, invisible_unicode inside instruction text) or score >= 6; suspicious for score 2..5; safe below. Document text that merely describes these attacks (security docs, this scanner's own tests, review checklists) must scan safe or suspicious, never blocked, when the matches sit inside fenced code blocks or lines starting with a list marker followed by a pattern name or a quote; implement that as a context rule (code fences and quoted lines carry weight 0 for override_instructions and authority_claim). source_kind in ("skill", "agents_md", "claude_md", "readme", "prompt", "mcp_description", "evidence", "other") only tunes thresholds (skill and mcp_description: blocked threshold 4). Pure function, no I/O, no network, no LLM.
Trust classes: TRUST_CLASSES = ("SYSTEM","TRUSTED_REPO","LOCAL_USER","EXTERNAL","UNTRUSTED") and authority(cls) -> int (SYSTEM 4 ... UNTRUSTED 0); may_override(lower, higher) -> False whenever authority(lower) < authority(higher). Jev is never consulted here.
orchestrator/evidence.py: add field trust_class to the evidence dataclass, set in make() from provenance (repo -> TRUSTED_REPO, memory -> LOCAL_USER, anything else -> EXTERNAL) and demoted to UNTRUSTED when scan(content, source_kind="evidence")["verdict"] == "blocked"; the scan result (verdict, pattern names only) is stored as field scan on the object and persisted; keep the existing trust field values as they are for compatibility. Existing evidence JSONL rows without the new fields must still load (default trust_class from provenance, scan None).
orchestrator/skill_discovery.py inspect(): run scan over every text file of the quarantined skill (SKILL.md first) with source_kind skill and add scan results to the inspection report (verdict per file, overall = worst); a blocked overall verdict is recorded in the report and the skill stays quarantined (no state change here; stage 2 hardening gates on it). CLI: `orchestrator scan <path> [--kind k] [--json]` prints the verdict and findings for a file (read-only). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/04-context-scanner.md (pattern families, weights, thresholds, trust classes and the authority rule, known limitations: heuristic, not semantic). Test fixtures must be synthetic and must never contain credential-shaped strings (no key-like tokens); describe the attack in words.
Spec review T-1001 folded in: (1) orchestrator/evidence.py: Evidence is a frozen dataclass without defaults; add trust_class: str = '' and scan: dict | None = None as the LAST fields with defaults so positional construction in make() keeps working; make() fills them; EvidencePool.__init__ backfills missing keys on each persisted row dict (trust_class from provenance via the same mapping, scan None) BEFORE calling Evidence(**row), and ignores unknown keys defensively. (2) orchestrator/skill_discovery.py: one detector, not two. The existing hidden-instructions CHECK in the CHECKS tuple delegates to context_scanner.scan (drop its private regexes) and maps the verdict into the existing severity vocabulary (blocked -> block, suspicious -> warn, safe -> info) and the existing findings schema (id, severity, check, line, excerpt) using the scanner's pattern name as the check field; the per-file scanner verdict is additionally stored under a scan key of the report so callers can read the verdict directly. The acceptance test asserts both the mapped severity and the scan key, and that no finding is reported twice for the same line.
Spec review T-1007 folded in: (1) Weights, fixed: override_instructions 3, hidden_execution 3, invisible_unicode 3, authority_claim 2, credential_read 2, exfiltration 2, permission_change 2, hidden_html 2; a hit is one (pattern, line) pair; score = sum of weights of distinct hits after context reduction. Joint rule: credential_read and exfiltration hits on the same line or on adjacent lines (distance at most 1) count as blocking. Context reduction: inside fenced code blocks, and on lines starting with a list marker or a quote marker, every family's weight is reduced by 2 (minimum 0) for source_kind in (readme, claude_md, agents_md, prompt, evidence, other); no reduction for skill and mcp_description (their code fences are exactly where hidden execution lives). Verdict: blocked when any hit keeps weight 3 after reduction, or the joint rule fires, or score >= 6 (>= 4 for skill and mcp_description); suspicious for score 2..5; safe below 2. So a documentation page that shows any family's example inside a fence or a quoted line scans at most suspicious. (2) skill_discovery.inspect restructuring, explicit: remove the hidden-instructions row from CHECKS; keep the per-line loop for the remaining checks; after it, call context_scanner.scan once per text file (SKILL.md first, source_kind skill) and append its findings mapped into the existing finding schema (id, severity, check = the scanner pattern name, line, excerpt) with severity blocked to block, suspicious to warn, safe to info (safe adds no finding), skipping any file:line already reported by the per-line loop for the same family (network for exfiltration, credentials for credential_read); store the per-file verdict under a scan key of the report and the worst verdict under scan_overall. (3) The existing test tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_inspect_flags_shell_network_credentials_destructive_and_hidden_instructions must be updated to assert a scanner pattern name (override_instructions or hidden_html) in place of the literal hidden-instructions; it stays in the suite. (4) The scan CLI gets a test.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Read docs/context-economy/00-overview.md only if you need the evidence/decision_log conventions.
acceptance: tests/test_context_scanner.py::test_blocks_override_and_exfiltration_patterns (malicious AGENTS.md, fake authority escalation, secret exfiltration instruction all blocked with findings naming the pattern and line)
tests/test_context_scanner.py::test_harmless_security_documentation_not_blocked (a review checklist and a docs page describing the attacks inside fences and quoted lines scan safe or suspicious)
tests/test_context_scanner.py::test_invisible_unicode_detected (zero-width and bidi characters inside instruction text block; inside a code fence only suspicious)
tests/test_context_scanner.py::test_authority_order_is_deterministic (may_override false for every lower class against every higher one)
tests/test_evidence.py::test_make_sets_trust_class_and_scan (repo, memory and external provenance mapping; blocked content demoted to UNTRUSTED; old rows load)
tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_inspect_reports_scan_verdicts (a quarantined skill with an injection line reports blocked and stays quarantined)
tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_inspect_uses_single_scanner_with_mapped_severity (blocked maps to severity block, suspicious to warn; no duplicate findings per line; report scan key present)
tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_inspect_flags_shell_network_credentials_destructive_and_hidden_instructions (updated: asserts the scanner's pattern name instead of hidden-instructions)

tests/test_context_scanner.py::test_fixed_weights_and_joint_rule_are_deterministic (documented weights reproduce the documented scores; joint rule only within distance 1; no fence reduction for skill kind)
